comment.body:
One compatibility constraint is worth locking down before implementing this: `importlib.metadata.packages_distributions()` is a natural fit for mapping top-level imports to distributions (including namespace packages), but the Python docs mark it **new in 3.10**, while pipreqs currently declares/supports Python 3.9 and its tox matrix includes `py39`. A direct stdlib switch would therefore regress a supported interpreter unless there is a 3.9-compatible fallback/backport strategy.

For a 3.9-compatible path, `importlib.metadata` already exposes distribution metadata and installed file lists. That can avoid parsing the `*.dist-info` directory name for `name`/`version`, but the docs also explicitly say the files API can return `None` when RECORD/SOURCES.txt is missing, so file-based top-level inference needs a defined fallback too.

References:
- Python 3.10 `packages_distributions()` (new in 3.10): https://docs.python.org/3.10/library/importlib.metadata.html#package-distributions
- Python 3.9 `importlib.metadata` file-list behavior: https://docs.python.org/3.9/library/importlib.metadata.html#distribution-files
- pipreqs currently requires `>=3.9,<3.14`: https://github.com/bndr/pipreqs/blob/48dbafd39003b9de177b8d314795e45797555850/pyproject.toml

I would make the regression explicitly cover a modern-backend wheel with no `top_level.txt` on Python 3.9 as well as 3.10+, and add a namespace-package case if the implementation derives import names from installed files. SECURITY-N/A; this is an API/backward-compatibility concern.

fallback.note: Direct GitHub issue comment write was denied by the integration after current-state, overlap, compatibility, and source verification.
